key_insight: Symmetry-preserving quantum circuits can still be trapped in invariant subspaces, but residual Lie-algebra analysis identifies added generators that restore accessibility.
engineering_relevance: Screening generators before optimization can guide symmetry-preserving circuit design and avoid ansätze with structural fidelity limits.
method: Identify residual commutants, invariant blocks, and conserved populations to bound target-state fidelity.
Screen added generators by the blocks they couple and the adjoint modules they generate.
Use real and complex coupling criteria to enlarge the dynamical algebra, with connected block graphs guiding multi-block designs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports algebraic proofs and demonstrations in XXZ and Hubbard models, but provides no quantitative performance benchmarks.
watch_item: Removing algebraic accessibility obstructions does not by itself guarantee shallow circuits, noise robustness, or efficient variational optimization.
paper_title: Residual-Algebraic Design of Symmetry-Preserving Variational Quantum Circuits
